---
title: "Appbay"
description: "A control plane for the Docker Compose apps you already run"
toc: false
---

Appbay manages Docker Compose apps — ingress, TLS, authentication, secrets and
namespacing — without taking your Compose files away from you.

You can **eject any app at any time** and run it with plain `docker compose up`. Appbay adds
structure; it never locks you in.

## Try it

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kundeng/appbay-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
appbay setup --domain home.lan
```

That installs a single binary — no Node.js, no Bun, nothing else on the host — then walks you
through creating the install, its secret vault, and the reverse proxy.

[Getting Started →](guide/quickstart.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| **Your Compose files stay yours** | Upstream files are never modified. Appbay layers policy on top and renders a new file. |
| **Traits instead of label soup** | `type: ingress` gives an app a hostname, TLS and forward-auth, rather than a dozen hand-written proxy labels. |
| **Secrets that never reach disk in the clear** | An encrypted local vault, with five injection modes depending on how the app expects to read them. |
| **One API, two interfaces** | The CLI and the web UI call the same code, so they cannot disagree about what your system is doing. |
| **Docker or Podman** | Choose the runtime once, at `init`. Rootful Podman on RHEL-family hosts is supported and tested, SELinux included. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Alpha

Appbay is alpha. The runtimes verified end-to-end are **Docker** and **rootful Podman**;
rootless Podman runs apps but cannot own the edge's ports. See
[Getting Started](guide/quickstart.qmd) for the specifics, including the RHEL-family notes.
:::
